facts.fact: Lot 18 小皮箱的箱盖压印 Mimi 外祖父的姓名缩写 "M. B."，她与外祖父共用这对缩写。
facts.anchor: The lid is embossed with Mimi’s grandfather’s initials, ‘M. B.’, which she shared.

facts.fact: Nancy 葬礼翌晨 Caswell 太太上门，Miriam 隔门偷听到 "untenable" 与 "Harold"（美式口音），Ma 真挚致哀。
facts.anchor: The morning after Nancy’s funeral, hushed female voices washed into the kitchen from the cobbled backyard. I crept closer to the door, caught the words ‘untenable’ and ‘Harold’ – American accent – then my mother’s sincere voice: ‘I understand, and I am so very sorry for your loss, Mrs Caswell.’

facts.fact: 前夜 Pa 把 "Alf 咕哝 Lawrence 之名" 当成指纹级铁证，无视证据推演天台一幕：Lawrence 因 Alf 说破其母与友人有染而动手。
facts.anchor: Pa had seized on Pamela’s fevered news that Alf had mumbled Lawrence’s name. As damning as a fingerprint, he declared. From there he spun the rooftop scene, contrary to all evidence: Lawrence lashed out when Alf stupidly told him his mother was sleeping with his friend.

facts.fact: Celia 到访半小时后，Doris 系着地址牌的家门钥匙出现在后门台阶上；Pa 由暴怒转为孩子般的嚎哭。
facts.anchor: Half an hour after Celia’s visit, Doris’s house key, strung with a small address label, appeared on our back step. The kindness it represented, the proof of good in the world, finally moved Pa from fury to tears and he sobbed like a child in Ma’s arms.

facts.fact: 打包搬离当日，拆掉 Alf 做的书桌最难受；数小时内 Bramley 一家的痕迹被抹净。
facts.anchor: Taking apart my bedroom desk Alf had made was the worst bit. Within a few hours, every trace of the Bramleys was wiped like chalk from a board.

facts.fact: 河岸告别：Miriam 钻进紫杉树篱缺口，与已等在喷泉边、金发发亮的他（Lawrence）对望。
facts.anchor: Ducking into the gap in the yew hedge, I sensed I’d see him. And there he was by the fountain, already staring, as if willing me to emerge too, his hair glinting pale gold.

facts.fact: 小屋岁月：Pa 无业憋疯、从午饭起酗酒，还闯进最近的警察局指控警方掩盖真相、袒护有钱的 Caswell 家。
facts.anchor: Without a job, unable to deal with Alf’s injuries, Pa grew stir-crazy. He drank. He drank a lot, starting at lunch. Then, one day he barrelled into the nearest police station and accused them of a cover-up, the local force pandering to the rich Caswells.

facts.fact: "Mimi" 这个自我像抖落的土从 Miriam 身上剥落，随后她也消失了。
facts.anchor: Mimi started to slough from me, like soil from the roots of a shaken dug-up plant, leaving only Miriam. Then she vanished too.

facts.fact: 霜晨 Miriam 一边对自己撒谎"最难的部分已过去"，一边手忙脚乱收拾外祖父旧皮箱：几件衣服、Whipple 的信、伦敦电话号码、微薄积蓄。
facts.anchor: The hard part was over, I lied to myself, as I frantically packed my grandfather’s old leather suitcase, my few nice clothes, Whipple’s letter, his precious London phone number, my meagre savings.

facts.fact: 出走晨摊牌：Pamela 嘶声怒斥 "Shame on you"。
facts.anchor: ‘Shame on you, Miriam,’ hissed Pamela. ‘Shame on you.’

facts.fact: Ma 捧住 Miriam 的脸低声放行：也许是在犯大错，但这是你自己可犯的错。
facts.anchor: Ma moved towards me, held my face in her hands and whispered, ‘You may be making the most terrible mistake, but it is yours to make, Miriam.’

facts.fact: Miriam 说爱全家却不放包、抓得更紧；一踏进冷雾小巷就知道再也不会回来。
facts.anchor: ‘Pa, I love you. All of you,’ I said, but didn’t set the bag down, only gripped it tighter. ‘I’m not going for ever.’ Yet the moment I stepped into the cold, foggy lane, I knew I was.
